conventions: Supplied English *have*: place it by what the clause writes, running rule 43's subtraction. Where a finite verb stands and the ASV renders it as *have* plus a complement carrying its lexeme, the whole phrase is that verb's one light-verb unit under rule 44 and heads on the complement — 28.19 יִשְׂבַּע → *shall have plenty of* and *shall have ... enough*. Where a written noun is recast as a head noun and a relative clause of having, the *have* is that noun's under rule 43's nominal-recasting paragraph — 28.22 אִישׁ רַע עָיִן → *He that hath an evil eye*, headed on *hath*. Where the clause writes neither, and its predicate adjective already holds its own English, the word answers to no morpheme and is `added` — 28.27 רַב מְאֵרוֹת → *shall have many a curse*, with *shall ... many* on רַב and *have* `added`.

The relational *of* or *with* the ASV writes between a predicate and the nominal completing it is placed by MACULA's morphology, not by the English shape. Where the head is tagged construct and the nominal is its nomen rectum, the word is the chain's own relation and belongs to the rectum under rule 19: 28.17 דַם־נָפֶשׁ → *the blood of any person*, 28.20 רַב־בְּרָכוֹת → *shall abound with blessings*, 28.21 פַּת־לֶחֶם → *a piece of bread*, 28.25 רְחַב־נֶפֶשׁ → *of a greedy spirit*. Where the nominal is absolute and the head a verb or participle reaching it, the word answers to the English predicate's valency and joins the predicate's unit under rule 44: 28.7 רֹעֶה זוֹלְלִים → *a companion of gluttons*, 28.19 יִשְׂבַּע־לָחֶם → *plenty of bread*, 28.21 הַכֵּר־פָּנִים → *respect of persons*, 28.23 מַחֲלִיק לָשׁוֹן → *flattereth with the tongue*.

A possessive the ASV supplies with no suffix in the phrase is `added` under rule 18's closing sentence wherever it determines a noun the Hebrew writes — 28.2 *the state thereof*, 28.6 and 28.18 *in his ways*, 28.16 *shall prolong his days*. It is not `added` where it stands inside a single morpheme's own fixed English rendering on a noun the Hebrew does not write: 28.25 בוֹטֵחַ → *he that putteth his trust*, where *trust* is the light-verb complement carrying the participle's lexeme under rule 44 and the *his* is what the English formula requires, exactly as rule 30 takes the pronouns of נָא's *I beseech thee* from the particle. Read whether a Hebrew noun stands under the possessive before marking it.
report: Read all 36 candidate groups and then the full dump end to end, since the table is keyed by source lemma and this chapter marks 13 supplied English words `added`. No cross-verse split found: every multi-treatment bucket differs because the ASV differs or because a different source morpheme stands in the clause. patches is empty.

Supplied *have* occurs four times and is placed three ways — inside a finite verb's own light-verb rendering (28.19 *shall have plenty of*, *shall have ... enough*), inside a written noun's recasting as a relative clause of having (28.22 אִישׁ → *He that hath*), and `added` where the verbless clause's predicate adjective already holds its own English (28.27 רַב → *shall ... many*). The discriminator is what the clause writes — a verb, a noun of possession, or neither — which is rule 43's own subtraction test, and 28.27 is that rule's יוֹסֵף חֲבָלִים shape. Recorded as a convention.

The relational *of* / *with* between a predicate and its complement is placed by MACULA's construct tagging: on the nomen rectum under rule 19 at 28.17, 28.20, 28.21b and 28.25, and inside the verb's unit under rule 44 at 28.7, 28.19, 28.21a and 28.23. The 28.20 verse pass already carries a correction onto this line and the other seven agree with it, so nothing is outstanding.

The supplied possessive is `added` wherever it stands on a written Hebrew noun (28.2 *thereof*, 28.6 *his*, 28.16 *his*, 28.18 *his*) and stays with the verb at 28.25, where *his* stands on *trust*, a light-verb complement the Hebrew writes no noun for. Rule 18's closing sentence targets a possessive on a written noun, so it does not reach 28.25; the reasoning there is rule 30's נָא sentence read for a light-verb idiom.

Two same-word pairs checked and left as accepted: the supplied *man* is the substantival participle's at 28.1 (rule 46) and `added` at 28.17 (rule 17, a finite verb with no nominal); and the waw of 28.3 is `unrepresented` because rule 41 gives the one written *that* to the articleless attributive participle beside it, while the second waw of the same verse takes *which* under rule 17, where nothing else in the clause licenses it.

BSB: all three disagreements are documented convention differences, not errors. 28.3 וְ — rule 41 takes the relative; 28.17 בְ — rule 40, the object promoted to a bare English object in *stay him*; 28.26 הוּא — rule 20's tripartite clause, the ASV realizing the subject once. No accepted edge was changed.

No promotion. The one place the contract is thin — a possessive an English light-verb idiom requires where the Hebrew writes no noun under it — rests on a single occurrence here, and none of the corpus tables supplied bear on בָטַח or on *put ... trust*. A rule on one verse would be paid for by every chapter after it, so it is logged as a convention instead.
